question: What minimum vertical clearance is required for overhead signs over the pavement and shoulders?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Overhead signs must provide a minimum vertical clearance of 17 feet to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, unless the mounting structure or nearby structures have a lesser vertical clearance. Reduced clearances are permitted in limited circumstances, such as near lower structures or in tunnels, and the 17-foot dimension is also applied to certain median-barrier-mounted preferential lane signs that overhang the roadway. Standards (mandatory): - "Overhead signs shall provide a vertical clearance of not less than 17 feet to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, except where the structure on which the overhead signs are to be mounted or other structures along the roadway near the sign structure have a lesser vertical clearance." (shown on the Section 2A.15 page, [Image 2]) - "Signs that are post-mounted on a median barrier that overhang any portion of the traveled way shall be mounted with a vertical clearance that complies with that of overhead signs." ([Image 2]) - For the associated supports: "For overhead sign supports, the minimum lateral offset from the edge of the shoulder (or if no shoulder exists, from the edge of the pavement) to the near edge of overhead sign supports (cantilever or sign bridges) shall be 6 feet. Overhead sign supports shall have a barrier or crash cushion to shield them if they are within the clear zone." Options (permitted): - If the vertical clearance of other structures along the roadway near the sign structure is less than 16 feet, the vertical clearance to an overhead sign structure or support may be as low as 1 foot higher than the vertical clearance of the other structures to improve sign visibility ([Image 2]). - In special cases the clearance to overhead signs may be reduced if necessary because of substandard dimensions in tunnels and other major structures such as double-deck bridges ([Image 2]). - Where lateral clearance is limited, preferential lane regulatory signs post-mounted on a median barrier (72 inches or less in width) may be skewed up to 45 degrees or mounted higher, such that the vertical clearance to the bottom of the sign, light fixture, or structural support, whichever is lowest, is not less than 17 feet above any portion of the pavement and shoulders. - The same 17-foot minimum applies where warning signs (Section 2G.08) or preferential lane guide signs (Section 2G.10) on median barriers are mounted higher due to limited lateral clearance. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-2, Panel H ("Overhead sign"), depicts an overhead street name sign with a "17 ft MIN." vertical clearance to the pavement and a 6 ft minimum lateral offset from the shoulder to the support. - [Image 2] shows the Section 2A.15 Standard text requiring not less than 17 feet of vertical clearance over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, plus the Options for reduced clearance near lower structures and in tunnels. - [Image 3] and [Image 4] (Figure 2D-10, Sheets 1 and 2) illustrate examples of overhead guide signs mounted on sign bridges at an intersection but do not state clearance dimensions. - [Image 5] (Sections 2E.19–2E.20) notes that vertical clearance of overhead signs is discussed in Section 2A.15 and establishes the 6-foot lateral offset for overhead sign supports on freeways and expressways. Citations: - Section 2A.16 Standard §1 (p.59) - Section 2G.03 Option §14 (p.411) - Section 2G.08 Option §4 (p.419) - Section 2G.10 Option §18 (p.422) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Page 100 - Page 344
gold_answer: At least 17 feet, except where nearby structures or special constrained structures qualify for the specific exceptions in Section 2A.15.
